checks.note: All six per-run limits (steps, wall seconds, tokens, cost, tool calls/min, subagents) have finite values, loaded by Budget.for_run.

The harness enforces limits in code the model cannot reach. The loop calls check_step, charge_model and check_tool_call. BudgetExceeded is re-raised by execute_tool, then caught in run(), which audits it, alerts Slack and returns None. Wall time is only checked between steps, so one slow API call can overrun it, but the run still stops at the next step.

The extractor receives the parent's budget, calls check_subagent (capped at max_subagents), and charges steps, tokens, cost and tool calls to it. The extractor role only has read_document, so it cannot spawn nested agents, and MAX_TURNS caps its loop.

checks.quote: INSERT INTO spend_quota (scope, key, day, spent_usd)
checks.note: Daily spend and per-minute run-start quotas for user, tenant and fleet are kept in Postgres and counted across runs. Exceeding one raises BudgetExceeded.

note: I could not find a way to make any of the four checks fail; the only gap is that wall time is checked per step, not during a single API call.
